transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been really slow at work lately. My hands feel like they’re moving through glue—just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever. People have started noticing I’m not as quick as I used to be.
Have you noticed any shaking or tremor in your hands, especially when they are at rest and not being used?
I haven’t really noticed my hands shaking when I’m resting. It’s more that they just feel slow.
Have you been feeling sad, down, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest. It feels like there’s not much point in trying to build the life I’d been planning.
How long have you been noticing this combination of slowed movements and low mood—days, weeks, or months?
It’s been about a year and eight months. It started after my hours got cut and I started watching my savings drain away.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any new medications—especially antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs?
I’m not sure—I don’t think I’ve started anything new recently.
Have you or others noticed your face looking less expressive, or your muscles feeling stiff or rigid, rather than just slow?
I haven’t really noticed my face looking different or my muscles feeling stiff. I just feel slow sometimes.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold, gaining weight without changes in diet, having dry skin or hair, or constipation over this same period?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that standing out.
Before this current period started about a year and eight months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of low mood and slowed-down feeling in the past, at any other point in your life?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time like this before the past year and a half or so.
Have you noticed your voice becoming hoarser or your hair thinning more than usual over this time?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed my voice sounding hoarse, and I haven’t really seen more hair thinning than usual.
Since this started about 20 months ago, has your low mood and slowness been continuous the whole time, or have there been periods where you felt back to your normal self in between?
It’s been there most of the time, honestly. There have been shorter periods where the sadness wasn’t as strong, but I wouldn’t say I really felt fully back to normal in between.
Over this past year and eight months, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep or appetite—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or eating significantly more or less?
My appetite’s been lower. I’ll skip meals without really meaning to, then at night realize I’ve only had coffee and a few bites of food. My clothes have gotten looser.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of hopelessness, worthlessness, or thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but sometimes I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up… like nobody would have to deal with me anymore.
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts—like feeling convinced something bad is happening to you that others don't believe, or hearing/seeing things that others don't seem to notice?
Sometimes at the salon, when I’m sweeping or rinsing bowls, I hear a woman’s voice by the shampoo stations saying I’m ruining everything. But then I’ll look and nobody’s there, or the salon’s empty.
Do you hear that voice only during the times when you're feeling most depressed and slowed down, or does it also happen even when your mood feels a bit better?

It happened even before I got really depressed. For a few weeks I was getting up and functioning pretty normally, but I was hearing it already, and I was sure someone at the salon was messing with my schedule.
During those few weeks when you were functioning normally and heard the voice, were you completely free of the low mood and sadness, or was some depression still present, just less intense?

There was still some depression, I think, just not as bad. I was getting up and going to work, doing things normally, but I was already hearing the voice and feeling like someone at the salon was messing with my schedule.

Was there ever a period of at least two weeks where you heard that voice or felt suspicious about your schedule being messed with, but had absolutely no sadness, low energy, or depressed mood at all during that time?

I mean, before the depression really got bad, there were several weeks where I was up and functioning pretty normally, and I was already hearing the voice and sure someone was interfering with my schedule at the salon.

target_item.manifestation: Before the depression really took over, there was a stretch of several weeks when I was still getting up and functioning more normally, but I was already hearing the voice and feeling sure someone at the salon was interfering with my schedule.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether psychotic symptoms occurred during a period without a major depressive episode, clarifying the duration of psychosis in the absence of prominent mood symptoms.

patient.answer: There was still some depression, I think, just not as bad. I was getting up and going to work, doing things normally, but I was already hearing the voice and feeling like someone at the salon was messing with my schedule.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucination, paranoid ideas) predated the worsening of depression and persisted during a period of only mild depressive symptoms, suggesting psychosis is not entirely confined to the severe mood episode—favoring schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) over MDD with psychotic features (F32.3). However, since some depressive symptoms were still present (not a clean 2-week psychosis-only window), F32.3 cannot yet be excluded.

doctor.intent: Determine if psychotic symptoms have ever occurred for at least 2 weeks with no depressive symptoms at all, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from major depression with psychotic features
doctor.question: Was there ever a period of at least two weeks where you heard that voice or felt suspicious about your schedule being messed with, but had absolutely no sadness, low energy, or depressed mood at all during that time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Before the depression really took over, there was a stretch of several weeks when I was still getting up and functioning more normally, but I was already hearing the voice and feeling sure someone at the salon was interfering with my schedule.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether psychotic symptoms occurred for at least two weeks with no depressive symptoms present.

patient.answer: I mean, before the depression really got bad, there were several weeks where I was up and functioning pretty normally, and I was already hearing the voice and sure someone was interfering with my schedule at the salon.

inference.note: The patient endorsed several weeks of hallucinations and paranoid ideation occurring while functioning normally with little to no depressive symptoms, indicating psychotic symptoms present outside a mood episode. This supports schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) and argues against major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F32.3), which requires psychotic symptoms to occur only during mood episodes.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a major depressive episode (depressed mood, anhedonia, psychomotor slowing, appetite/weight loss, passive suicidal ideation) lasting ~20 months, alongside persistent auditory hallucinations (a derogatory voice) and persecutory delusions (belief coworkers were sabotaging her schedule). Critically, the psychotic symptoms emerged and persisted during a several-week period when depressive symptoms were minimal/subthreshold, indicating psychosis occurring independent of the mood episode—supporting schizoaffective disorder rather than major depression with psychotic features. The predominance of depressive symptoms over the overall course (with mood symptoms present most of the time) and absence of catatonia, thyroid symptoms, medication-induced parkinsonism, or purely substance-related cause further support F25.1 (depressive type) over primary psychotic or purely mood disorders.

confirmed_symptoms: Loss of motivation and hopelessness about future plans
Psychomotor slowing (slowed hand movements, difficulty with fine motor tasks at work)
Decreased appetite with unintentional weight loss (looser clothing)
Auditory hallucination of a woman's voice saying she is 'ruining everything' when no one is present
Persecutory delusion that a coworker was interfering with her schedule
Psychotic symptoms present even during a period when mood was only mildly depressed

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms ongoing for approximately 20 months, with mood symptoms present most of the time and psychotic symptoms co-occurring; a several-week period identified where psychotic symptoms persisted with only mild/subthreshold depression.
additional_requirements: No prior episodes of similar mood/psychomotor symptoms reported before this 20-month period
No evidence of hypothyroidism (denied cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin, hoarseness, hair thinning)
No parkinsonian features (denied resting tremor, rigidity, masked facies)
No recent antipsychotic or antiemetic medication exposure

Psychotic symptoms confirmed to occur independent of full mood episode for at least several weeks, though not entirely free of any depressive symptoms, supporting schizoaffective rather than mood disorder with psychotic features
